    The dimension inequality for Π(Δ) #

    Proof of Proposition 4.1, Step 2 (periodic-mesh-calculations.tex): "For each vertex i of Δ, put P_i = e_i Π(Δ), n_i = dim_k P_i ... There is an exact sequence P_i → ⊕_{j∼i} P_j → P_i → S_i → 0. The map onto rad P_i prefixes outgoing arrows. To identify its kernel, express a relation among the prefixed paths in the free path algebra as a sum of contextual defining relations. A nonempty initial context gives zero in the coefficient module after its first arrow. An empty initial context gives a right multiple of the single relation at i. These are exactly the images of the first map. ... dimensions give 2n_i - ∑_{j∼i} n_j = 1 + dim K_i > 0."

    We work with S i, the formal combinations of all paths starting at i, and its subspace I i spanned by the contextual relations starting at i, so that P_i = S i / I i. Only the inequality ∑_{j∼i} n_j ≤ 2 n_i - 1 is used later.

    This file: first-arrow decompositions of paths.

    theorem Quiver.Path.nil_or_first {V : Type v} [Quiver V] {i v : V} (u : Path i v) :
    (∃ (h : i = v), u = h ▸ nil) ∨ ∃ (j : V) (a : i ⟶ j) (u' : Path j v), u = a.toPath.comp u'

    A path is empty or begins with an arrow.

    theorem Quiver.Path.toPath_comp_vertices {V : Type v} [Quiver V] {i j v : V} (a : i ⟶ j) (u : Path j v) :
    (a.toPath.comp u).vertices = i :: u.vertices
